pros.claim: Naming the unprotected set early prevents the worst conversation in this business, which is discovering the gap during a loss
pros.example: telling a client at the start that their vertical application's data has no export path, so the gap becomes a funded decision rather than a discovery on the day the vendor's service fails

pros.claim: An honest recoverable-set statement makes every downstream number defensible, from questionnaires to renewal conversations
pros.example: an insurer questionnaire item answered precisely because the protected and unprotected sets were already written down

cons.claim: Publishing the gaps weakens the perceived completeness of the service and invites price comparison against providers who never mention them
cons.example: a competitor's proposal that says everything is backed up sitting beside a statement that lists three things that are not

cons.claim: Gap statements age quickly as clients adopt new applications without telling the provider
cons.example: a new cloud tool bought by the office manager that holds business records nobody has assessed

failure_modes: assuming a cloud platform's native retention is a backup
letting the statement be written once during deployment and never refreshed
burying the gaps in a technical appendix the owner will never read
keeping the only copy of encryption keys or recovery codes inside the environment they protect
acceptance_tests: a current recoverable-set statement exists in client-facing language naming what comes back, how far back and what does not come back at all
each named gap is linked to a funded remediation or an entry in the accepted-risk register with a date
the statement's last review date falls within the agreed refresh interval
revisit_triggers: the client adopts a new application or changes a platform plan
a drill or verification reveals a gap the statement did not list
a vendor changes native retention, export capability or immutability options

base.update_signal: a new application, a plan change, or a drill finding changes what is genuinely recoverable

nodes.definition: Run the standing rhythm that keeps the subscription visible in the long stretches when nothing dramatic happens. The interval is matched to what the tier actually funds - a short monthly check-in for larger accounts, a quarterly session for most small ones - and the agenda is driven by the evidence the operation already produces rather than by whatever is top of mind: coverage and estate drift, the alert and incident picture with closure reasons, patch and configuration state, backup verification and drill results, awareness-training completion, the accepted-risk register, and the decisions the practice needs from the client. It ends with a short list of decisions and owners, not with a deck. The rhythm exists to prevent two specific failures: the invisible provider whose value nobody can articulate when the renewal lands on a new financial decision-maker's desk, and the review that quietly turns into a sales meeting, which teaches the client that every conversation costs money.

included: the review interval matched to the funded tier and who attends
the evidence-driven standing agenda and the decisions-and-owners output
the rule that the review is not a sales meeting
excluded: the construction of the report artifact itself
the framework mapping produced on request
the renewal negotiation

pros.claim: A predictable rhythm converts invisible work into a relationship with the person who signs the renewal
pros.example: a quarterly session that has already introduced the practice to the incoming office manager before she reviews the recurring charges

pros.claim: An evidence-driven agenda makes the meeting short and decision-producing rather than a status recital
pros.example: a thirty-minute review that ends with three owner decisions on multi-factor coverage, an unsupported machine and the next drill date

cons.claim: Review time is unbilled labor that scales with the client count and competes with the queue
cons.example: a book of small clients where quarterly reviews consume a full week of technician and owner time each quarter

cons.claim: Small-business owners frequently cancel a meeting about a problem that is not currently hurting them
cons.example: three consecutive rescheduled reviews at a client with no incidents, ending in a renewal conversation with no shared history

failure_modes: reviews that happen only when something goes wrong
an agenda of vendor dashboards instead of decisions
attending with the technical contact only, so the person who signs never hears any of it
using the review to introduce an upsell, which trains the client to avoid the meeting
acceptance_tests: each client has a stated review interval matched to their tier, and the last review date falls inside it
each review produces a written decision list with owners and dates, distributed to the client
the standing agenda items are all covered or explicitly deferred with a reason
revisit_triggers: two consecutive reviews are missed or rescheduled
the client's decision-maker changes
the tier or scope changes what the review should cover
an incident or drill result requires an out-of-cycle session

base.update_signal: missed reviews, a change of decision-maker, or a scope change alters the rhythm the relationship needs

nodes.definition: Assemble the recurring report that makes invisible work visible without manufacturing fear, built entirely from artifacts the operation already produces so that reporting is a compilation task rather than a creative one. Its sections are stable: coverage, meaning assets monitored against assets known with the blind spots named; hygiene state, meaning patch and configuration status, backup verification results, drill outcomes with measured times, and training completion; the event picture, meaning what was triaged, what was acted on, what was declared and how it ended, with closure reasoning available; delivery against the stated commitment, including targets missed and why; open risks with owners and dates; and an explicit note of what the practice did not get to this period. Every number states what it counts, its denominator and what it does not prove, and the report carries the standing residual-risk sentence. The test of a good report is behavioural: an owner who reads it can say in their own words what they are getting and what is still exposed, and nothing in it made them more frightened than the evidence warrants.

included: the fixed report sections compiled from existing operational artifacts
metric honesty rules covering denominator, definition and limits
reporting misses, gaps and undone work as first-class content
excluded: framework or questionnaire mapping, which is a separate bounded product
the renewal or expansion conversation
the technical detail of individual alerts

pros.claim: A report built from existing artifacts costs little and is impossible to challenge, because every line points at a dated record
pros.example: a coverage line that resolves to the reconciliation output and a restore line that resolves to the last verification artifact

pros.claim: Reporting what was missed builds more credibility than reporting only successes, and it surfaces resourcing problems while they are still small
pros.example: stating that two patch cycles slipped and what changes as a result, which turns into a client decision rather than a later discovery

cons.claim: An honest report is less impressive than a vendor dashboard and can make a quiet, well-run period look like nothing happened
cons.example: a period with no incidents where the strongest content is a successful drill and an unchanged risk register

cons.claim: Compilation still costs recurring hours the tier must fund, and it grows with the number of clients rather than with revenue per client
cons.example: a monthly report for every client in a book of small accounts consuming more time than the accounts individually justify

failure_modes: reporting vendor-generated threat counts because they look impressive
omitting missed commitments and undone work to keep the report positive
sending a report nobody reads instead of walking through the decisions in the review
metrics whose denominator changes silently between periods so trends are meaningless
acceptance_tests: every section of the report traces to a dated operational artifact rather than to a narrative written for the occasion
each metric states its definition, denominator and limits, and the residual-risk sentence is present
misses, gaps and undone work appear in the report for any period in which they occurred
revisit_triggers: a client says the report does not tell them what they are getting
a metric is challenged as misleading or its denominator changes
the service scope changes what should be reported
the reporting effort outgrows what the tier funds

base.update_signal: client feedback, a challenged metric, or a scope change alters what the report must contain to be both honest and useful

nodes.definition: Translate the evidence the service already produces into the language of whatever control list the client is facing - an insurer's renewal questionnaire, a larger customer's vendor-security review, a sector framework's control families, a contract's security schedule - so the client can answer accurately, and stop precisely at that line. The practice supplies factual, dated statements about what is deployed, configured, verified and drilled, each pointing at the artifact behind it, and it says clearly what is not in place. It does not certify, audit, assess or attest; it does not sign the client's questionnaire or answer in the client's name; it does not opine on whether the client is compliant; and it flags that requirements differ by jurisdiction, sector, carrier and contract and change over time, so the client's counsel, assessor or carrier must verify the current position and make the determination. A row that no artifact supports is answered as not in place, never dressed up as partially or in progress to make a questionnaire pass, because an inaccurate answer to an insurer can be far more expensive to the client than an honest gap.

included: mapping existing dated evidence onto the client's control list or questionnaire language
the explicit refusal set covering certification, attestation, signature and compliance opinion
the verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction flag and the unsupported-row rule
excluded: formal assessment, audit or certification of any framework
interpreting insurance coverage or advising on a claim
legal determination of statutory or contractual duties

pros.claim: Mapping is high-value low-cost work because the evidence already exists and the client cannot easily produce it themselves
pros.example: answering a customer's vendor-security review in an afternoon from verification artifacts and the coverage map

pros.claim: The stated boundary keeps the practice out of a liability class it is neither licensed nor insured for
pros.example: declining to sign an attestation section and directing it to the client's officer and counsel while still supplying every underlying fact

cons.claim: Clients experience the boundary as unhelpfulness at the moment they are under deadline pressure from an insurer or a customer
cons.example: an owner asking the practice to just tick the boxes because the renewal is due on Friday

cons.claim: Honest not-in-place answers can cost the client a policy term or a contract, and the practice gets the blame for the gap it merely reported
cons.example: a questionnaire answered accurately leading to a coverage condition the owner did not expect

failure_modes: softening an unsupported row to help a questionnaire pass
letting a mapping document drift into language that reads as certification
answering in the client's name or completing the form on their behalf
presenting a framework mapping as evidence that the client is compliant
acceptance_tests: every mapped row points at a dated artifact or is answered as not in place

the document carries the explicit statement that it is not an audit, assessment, attestation or legal advice and that requirements must be verified currently in the client's jurisdiction and contracts
no questionnaire or attestation in the record was signed or submitted by the practice on the client's behalf
revisit_triggers: the client's carrier, customer or contract issues a new or changed control list
a framework version or a jurisdiction's requirements change
an artifact behind a mapped row expires or fails verification

base.update_signal: a changed questionnaire, framework version or jurisdictional requirement, or an expired artifact behind a mapped row

nodes.definition: Keep one living list of the exposures that remain open because the client declined, deferred, or cannot yet fund the fix: the ancient machine running the workshop's only supported version of a controller application, the shared reception login the office refuses to give up, the owner who will not enable multi-factor authentication on their own account, the vertical application whose vendor forbids current operating systems, the blind spot from the coverage map. Each entry records the exposure in plain operational terms, the recommended control, the client's decision and its date, who made it, any compensating control in place, and a review date. Its tone is the same neutral evidence-bounded language used everywhere else: it describes what an exposure makes possible, not a dramatized loss scenario, and it invents no probabilities. It is re-presented at each review so a deferral cannot silently become permanent, and it protects both parties later - the client because the decision and its context are recorded rather than reconstructed after an incident, and the practice because the record exists without ever having to be brandished.

included: the entry structure covering exposure, recommendation, decision, decision-maker, date, compensating control and review date
re-presentation of open entries at each review
the neutral-language rule and the ban on invented probabilities
excluded: pricing or selling the remediation an entry implies
deciding for the client whether a risk is acceptable
any use of the register as leverage during a dispute or a renewal

pros.claim: Recording the decision at the time it is made removes the worst post-incident argument, which is whether anyone ever raised it
pros.example: an entry from two quarters earlier showing the multi-factor recommendation, the owner's decision and the date, available without anyone having to reconstruct a memory

pros.claim: Re-presenting open items converts a one-time refusal into a repeated, low-pressure decision that often changes over time
pros.example: a deferred item accepted at the third review because the client's own customer began asking about it

cons.claim: A register can be experienced as a running list of the client's failures, which sours the relationship if the tone slips
cons.example: an owner who feels lectured every quarter about the same machine they cannot afford to replace

cons.claim: It is easy for the register to become a defensive instrument rather than a decision aid, which corrodes trust the moment the client notices
cons.example: referring to the register during a dispute in a way that reads as we told you so

failure_modes: entries with no decision-maker, no date or no review date
dramatized descriptions or invented likelihood figures added to increase pressure
keeping the register internal so the client never sees what they are carrying
letting entries accumulate without ever being closed, reworded or re-scoped
acceptance_tests: every open entry names the exposure, the recommendation, the decision, the decision-maker, the date, any compensating control and a review date
the register is presented at each review and the presentation is recorded
no entry contains a probability figure or loss estimate that is not traceable to a stated source
revisit_triggers: an entry reaches its review date
an incident touches an accepted risk
the client's circumstances, insurer conditions or customer requirements change what is acceptable
a compensating control changes or lapses

base.update_signal: a review date, an incident touching an accepted risk, or a change in the client's obligations reopens an entry

nodes.definition: Manage the structural paradox of this business: when the service works, the client experiences nothing, and nothing is hard to keep paying for. Churn pressure arrives in recognizable forms - a quiet year, a cheaper quote promising more, a new bookkeeper or finance director reviewing recurring charges, a merger, or an owner who has concluded from the absence of incidents that the risk was overstated. The counter is evidence, never fear: the artifact trail of verified restores and measured drills, coverage and drift reconciliations, patch and training state, incidents detected and handled with their timelines, and the accepted-risk register showing what the client themselves chose to carry; plus a reminder of the shared responsibility split, since much of what kept them safe was work they never saw. Scope or price changes are explained as mechanisms from the operator's own measured cost to serve - seats and sites added, alert load, tooling cost, incident labor consumed - rather than as an annual increase with no story. Two things are forbidden: defending a renewal by escalating threat language, and punishing an exit; a departing client is offboarded cleanly with their data, documentation, credentials and monitoring history handed back.

included: recognizing churn signals and assembling the evidence pack that answers them
explaining scope and price changes as measured cost-to-serve mechanisms
the ban on fear-based retention and the clean offboarding and handback obligation
excluded: the original pricing architecture and tier design
expansion offers, which the evidence-driven scope-growth unit owns
any assertion about what a competitor's cheaper offer does or does not include beyond verifiable facts

pros.claim: An artifact trail lets a new financial decision-maker evaluate the service on evidence rather than on the absence of drama
pros.example: handing an incoming finance director the last four reviews, two measured drills and an incident timeline instead of an argument about why security matters

pros.claim: A mechanism-based price explanation survives scrutiny that an unexplained increase would not
pros.example: showing seat growth, added applications and the resulting measured alert load as the reason a tier changes at renewal

cons.claim: Evidence loses to price when the buyer has decided the category is a commodity, and no amount of honesty changes that
cons.example: losing a renewal to a quote that names the same tool set at a lower price with no mention of who watches the queue

cons.claim: Clean offboarding costs unbilled hours and hands a successor everything they need to take over smoothly
cons.example: packaging documentation, credentials and monitoring history for a competitor who won on price

failure_modes: reaching renewal with no accumulated evidence because reviews were skipped in quiet quarters
answering a price challenge with threat language or implied consequences of leaving
an unexplained annual increase that reads as opportunism
withholding data, credentials or documentation from a departing client
acceptance_tests: each renewal is supported by an evidence pack assembled from dated artifacts covering the term, not from narrative
any scope or price change states the measured mechanism that produced it
the offboarding checklist for any departing client shows data, documentation, credentials and monitoring history returned, with dates
revisit_triggers: a churn signal appears, such as a price challenge, a change of financial decision-maker or a missed review sequence
the renewal window opens
measured cost to serve moves materially away from the current price
a client leaves, which should trigger an honest internal review of why

base.update_signal: churn outcomes, measured cost to serve, or a change in the client's decision-makers changes what the renewal case must contain

nodes.definition: Grow the account from what monitoring, incidents and drills actually revealed, in priority order of risk reduction per unit of client spend, with the no-fear-selling rule applying at full force inside an existing relationship where trust makes pressure far more effective and therefore far more corrosive. The legitimate sources of expansion are all observational: blind spots from the coverage map, repeated findings in post-incident reviews, a recoverable-set gap the client's own drill exposed, new sites, seats or applications found during reconciliation, and a control a client's insurer or larger customer has begun to expect. The rules are strict. Present the evidence and the residual risk in the same neutral language used everywhere else. Never time an offer to a live incident; findings are presented after stand-down in the ordinary review. Never withhold a cheap fix that falls inside current scope in order to make a paid tier look necessary. Where a client is plainly stretched, sequence the smallest effective step rather than the largest sellable one. Record a decline in the accepted-risk register without escalation of language and re-present it on its ordinary review date.

included: the observational sources that legitimately justify an expansion offer
the timing, language and sequencing rules that keep expansion pressure-free
recording declines in the register without escalation
excluded: the tier architecture and price of the expanded service
the initial sale to a new client
deployment of whatever the client agrees to add

pros.claim: Expansion grounded in the client's own evidence is easier to agree to and almost never regretted, which protects the renewal it sits inside
pros.example: adding protection for the application whose data the client's own drill showed could not be recovered

pros.claim: Refusing incident-timed offers preserves the trust that makes every future recommendation credible
pros.example: presenting the logging expansion three weeks after the incident in the ordinary review rather than in the week the owner was frightened

cons.claim: The self-imposed timing and language rules leave revenue on the table exactly when a client would most readily say yes
cons.example: an owner who would have approved anything during the incident approving only the smallest item a month later

cons.claim: Sequencing the smallest effective step slows the account's growth and can leave a serious gap open for longer
cons.example: a stretched client taking three quarters to reach a control that could have been bought at once

failure_modes: raising an upgrade while the client is still in an active incident
holding back an in-scope fix so a paid tier looks necessary
presenting a gap with dramatized consequences rather than the observed evidence
repeatedly re-raising a declined item outside its review date until the client agrees
acceptance_tests: each expansion offer cites the specific observation - coverage gap, review finding, drill result or reconciliation - that produced it
no offer is dated inside an open incident, and each declined item appears in the register with its ordinary review date
no item within current scope was deferred or withheld in order to support an offer
revisit_triggers: a review finding or drill result exposes a new gap
the estate grows or a new application class appears
a client's insurer or customer changes what they expect
a declined item reaches its review date

base.update_signal: new observed gaps, a change in the client's external requirements, or evidence that an offer was perceived as pressure

edges.why_related: the defensive boundary is meaningful only against a written statement of which systems and actions are inside the envelope, so the refusal list is derived from the authorization
what the practice may do without asking determines what it can honestly commit to doing out of hours, so the commitment is bounded by the standing authority
the claim vocabulary describes the service that was actually promised, so the coverage window and exclusions define what may honestly be said in a status update
telemetry may only be collected from systems the envelope covers, so the in-scope register defines the outer edge of the coverage map
tuning presupposes knowing which sources feed the queue and which are blind spots, otherwise a stream is tuned that never contained the critical signal
the severity model judges a stream that has already been characterized for this tenant, so tuning quality sets what triage actually sees
declaration is one of the dispositions the triage model can reach, so the declaration criteria extend the severity judgment rather than replacing it
declaration is what starts a runbook, so the runbooks are written against the declared-incident classes the criteria produce
the containment judgment happens at the decision points the runbook marks, using the ordered options the runbook already lists
what must be captured before remediation is specified per scenario inside the runbook, so preservation executes steps the runbook defines
declaration is the event that starts the client update rhythm and names the lead who will speak
escalation to carrier, counsel or a specialist is delivered through the established incident channel and lead rather than through an improvised conversation
the review can only reconstruct what was preserved, so the timeline is bounded by the exports, images and action logs captured during the incident
you can only verify the restorability of data sets you know exist and are protected, so the estate map defines what the regime must cover
a drill rehearses recovery from copies whose basic restorability has already been verified, otherwise the exercise only rediscovers a broken backup
the statement of what does not come back is written from what verification proved is actually inside the protected set
the standing review agenda opens with coverage and drift, which only exists because the reconciliation produces it
the report is the artifact the review is built on, so its sections and period follow the agreed rhythm
framework and questionnaire rows are answered from the dated evidence the recurring report already compiles rather than from fresh assertions
the register is re-presented on the review rhythm, which is what stops a deferral from becoming permanent by default
the renewal case is assembled from accumulated reports, so a term without reporting arrives at renewal with no evidence to present
open register entries are the legitimate inventory of expansion candidates and the place a decline is recorded without pressure
no runbook step may include an action outside the strictly defensive boundary, however tempting the trail is during the incident it describes
the containment option set is limited to pre-authorized actions plus whatever a named approver grants in the moment, which bounds the decision before judgment even starts
incident updates inherit the claim discipline, so no update may assert containment, cleanliness or a recovery time the evidence does not yet support
stopping the attacker quickly destroys exactly the volatile evidence that later explains what happened, while preserving first costs minutes during which harm continues
edges.resolution_rule: capture the cheap perishable artifacts inline while containing reversibly, since log export and a snapshot cost little; where the two genuinely cannot both be done, contain to stop active harm and record precisely what was lost, and never take an irreversible remediation step before the runbook's capture list when exfiltration, a claim or an external review is plausible

edges.why_related: the measured labor a tenant consumes can exceed what its price funds, which creates pressure to deliver less monitoring than was promised
edges.resolution_rule: the stated commitment holds until it is renegotiated in writing; an over-budget tenant is addressed by tuning within hygiene limits, fixing or funding the underlying condition, re-scoping, or repricing openly at renewal, and never by quietly reducing what is watched

edges.why_related: a suppression that makes the queue survivable can remove the very signal whose absence delays or prevents a declaration
edges.resolution_rule: no suppression may cover a signal combination the declaration criteria treat as observable evidence of attacker access; such a suppression requires a named approval, a compensating detection and a short review date, and any suppression found in an incident timeline is removed and the criteria re-tested

edges.why_related: bringing in a carrier, counsel or a specialist responder exposes the incident and the practice's own delivery to outside scrutiny and can cost the practice the relationship
edges.resolution_rule: escalate whenever a stated trigger is met regardless of commercial consequence; the client's exposure dominates the practice's account risk, and a concealed incident that later surfaces damages the relationship far more than an early referral while potentially jeopardizing the client's own claim

edges.why_related: disclosing the practice's own contribution to an incident is the honest act and simultaneously the most direct threat to the account it concerns
edges.resolution_rule: disclose the contribution in the same update in which it becomes known internally, paired with the concrete change that prevents recurrence; retention is rebuilt afterwards with evidence, and concealment is never available as an option even when the client would probably never find out

edges.why_related: expansion revenue is easiest to win with heightened threat language, which is exactly the vocabulary the claim discipline forbids
edges.resolution_rule: the claim discipline wins without exception: every expansion case is presented in the same neutral evidence-bounded language as the report, never inside a live incident, and a decline is recorded in the register and re-presented only on its ordinary review date

edges.why_related: tuning quality is the dominant driver of how many technician minutes a tenant consumes per seat, so the economics move when tuning moves
a measured, witnessed recovery is the single piece of evidence that most reliably converts an abstract subscription into something a small-business owner can see the value of
review findings that fall outside current scope are the legitimate origin of expansion offers, which is why their timing and language are constrained
incident findings are carried into the next standing review so that new-scope items are discussed in the ordinary rhythm rather than in the aftermath
the recoverable-set statement is refreshed and republished as part of each reporting period so the client's expectation stays current
what a drill discovers about missing dependencies and slow paths changes the verification rung, cadence and content for that client
a signal that was suppressed, missed or arrived too late sends the review's findings straight back into the tuning baseline and the suppression list
both are disciplines of proving in advance that a needed artifact will actually exist and be usable at the moment of demand, rather than trusting that a process ran

conflict_axes.name: containment_speed_vs_evidence_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Every minute spent capturing logs, rules and images is a minute the attacker keeps working, and every fast remediation destroys the record that would later explain what happened to an insurer, a customer or the client themselves.
poles: preserve the record before touching anything
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: contain reversibly while capturing the cheap perishable artifacts inline, and never take an irreversible step before the runbook's capture list when an external party may review the incident

conflict_axes.name: detection_sensitivity_vs_triage_cost
conflict_axes.description: A sensitive queue catches quiet identity attacks and consumes labor a fixed per-seat price must fund; a quiet queue is affordable and blind, and the tuning that separates them is the same lever in both directions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: suppress only characterized benign-normal with owner and expiry, protect the top-severity combinations absolutely, and solve remaining volume by fixing conditions, re-scoping or repricing rather than by looking less

conflict_axes.name: coverage_promise_vs_staffing_reality
conflict_axes.description: Small businesses want continuous protection and competitors advertise it, while a small practice has a handful of technicians who sleep; the gap can be closed by automation and honesty or papered over with language.
poles: promise the coverage the market expects
promise only what the roster can deliver
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state the coverage window, the out-of-hours automated path and the response definition explicitly, and let pre-authorized automated containment carry the hours no human is watching

conflict_axes.name: honest_uncertainty_vs_demand_for_certainty
conflict_axes.description: A frightened owner wants to be told they are safe, and the only truthful answers early in an incident are partial ones; reassurance bought with a premature all-clear has to be repaid with a retraction.
poles: state only what the evidence supports
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the four-part update structure so uncertainty arrives inside a visible plan, and treat we do not know yet plus what is being done as a complete answer

conflict_axes.name: self_disclosure_vs_account_preservation
conflict_axes.description: When a missed alert, an expired suppression or a lapsed patch formed part of the attack path, honesty is both the right action and a direct threat to the revenue that funds the practice.
poles: protect the account and the contract
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclose in the update where it becomes known internally, paired with the concrete corrective change, and rebuild the relationship with evidence rather than with silence

conflict_axes.name: escalation_vs_keeping_the_work
conflict_axes.description: Referring an incident to a carrier's panel, a specialist responder or counsel protects the client and simultaneously removes the practice from the most visible work, invites external scrutiny, and can end the relationship.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the trigger list as non-discretionary, hand over a preserved evidence package, and stay in the supporting role rather than competing with the specialist

conflict_axes.name: proving_value_vs_manufacturing_fear
conflict_axes.description: The easiest way to make a quiet quarter feel worth paying for is to dramatize the threat landscape, which is exactly the practice that destroys the client's ability to calibrate real risk and the provider's credibility with it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build the report from dated operational artifacts with denominators and limits, include misses and undone work, and let a successful drill rather than a threat count carry the value story

conflict_axes.name: useful_compliance_answers_vs_attestation_boundary
conflict_axes.description: Clients under questionnaire or contract deadlines want the provider to simply answer for them, and every step toward doing so moves the practice into assessment and attestation territory it is neither qualified nor insured to occupy.
poles: give the client the answers they need
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: supply dated factual statements tied to artifacts, answer unsupported rows as not in place, refuse signature and compliance opinion, and route the determination to the client's counsel, assessor or carrier

conflict_axes.name: drill_realism_vs_production_disruption
conflict_axes.description: The drills that reveal the most are the ones that disturb the business most, and a small client's tolerance for a disruptive exercise is limited, so realism is traded against the willingness to run it at all.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb the drill ladder over time, run disruptive stages in isolated environments or outside trading hours, and treat every discovered failure as the return that justifies the disruption

edge_cases.description: A high-severity identity alert fires at two in the morning, hours outside the coverage window, while the payroll run is scheduled for the same night
edge_cases.trigger: a top-severity signal arrives when no human is watching the queue
edge_cases.mitigation: let pre-authorized automated containment act immediately, page the on-call person against the written wake-someone criteria, and rely on the commitment having already told the client exactly what happens overnight so the response is judged against what was promised

edge_cases.description: The mailbox the practice is using to discuss the incident is the mailbox that is compromised, and the attacker is reading and deleting messages inside the thread
edge_cases.trigger: the incident channel runs through the affected system
edge_cases.mitigation: move to the pre-agreed out-of-band channel at declaration rather than after suspicion, verify the client contact by voice, and preserve the existing thread as evidence before any mailbox cleanup

edge_cases.description: The client demands that the practice access the attacker's mailbox, scan the supplier's network or trace the person who took the money
edge_cases.trigger: a client under financial loss asks for offensive or third-party action
edge_cases.mitigation: use the pre-written refusal paired with the routes that do exist - preserve evidence, report to the appropriate law-enforcement or fraud channel, involve the carrier and counsel, and harden the path that was used

edge_cases.description: Backup jobs have reported success for months, and the first real restore fails because an encryption key, a licence or an application dependency was never in the protected set
edge_cases.trigger: a restore is attempted for the first time under real conditions
edge_cases.mitigation: assign a verification rung above job status to every protected set, hold key and licence custody outside the protected environment, and treat a failed verification as an incident-grade finding rather than a maintenance note

edge_cases.description: The signal that would have caught the intrusion was suppressed a year earlier as noise by an engineer who has since left the practice
edge_cases.trigger: a post-incident timeline intersects an undocumented or expired suppression
edge_cases.mitigation: require owner, reason and expiry on every suppression, review the whole suppression set against the declaration criteria after any such finding, and disclose the suppression's role to the client in the review

edge_cases.description: The sign-in and audit logs needed to reconstruct the intrusion have already aged out of the client's cloud plan retention
edge_cases.trigger: dwell time exceeded the platform's native log retention window
edge_cases.mitigation: export perishable logs at declaration as a standing first action, record the retention limit as a named blind spot with a funded or accepted decision, and state plainly to the client and any specialist what can no longer be determined

edge_cases.description: Reconciliation finds devices and an entire second site in the estate that the provider was never told about, none of them hardened and none of them billed
edge_cases.trigger: the client grows or acquires without informing the provider
edge_cases.mitigation: raise the unmanaged assets as a security finding immediately, pass the seat and site drift to the account process as a true-up input, and record any part the client declines to bring in scope in the register

edge_cases.description: An insurer questionnaire asks a yes or no question whose honest answer is partly, and the client's renewal deadline is days away
edge_cases.trigger: a binary control question meets a partially implemented control
edge_cases.mitigation: supply the precise factual position with its artifact and let the client and their broker answer, never soften an unsupported row, and offer the remediation that would make the answer a clean yes on a stated timeline

edge_cases.description: The post-incident timeline shows that the practice's own closed alert or missed patch cycle was part of the attack path
edge_cases.trigger: the review implicates the provider's own delivery
edge_cases.mitigation: disclose it in the update where it becomes known, present the corrective change with an owner and a date, absorb the in-scope remediation without charge, and let the client decide about the relationship with full information

edge_cases.description: The owner who declined multi-factor authentication on their own account for two review cycles is the account that is taken over
edge_cases.trigger: an accepted risk becomes the incident
edge_cases.mitigation: run the incident without recrimination, reference the register only as a factual record of what was recommended and decided, and re-present the control as the first review finding rather than as vindication

edge_cases.description: A year with no incidents ends with a renewal challenged by a cheaper quote promising continuous monitoring
edge_cases.trigger: quiet performance meets price scrutiny from a new financial decision-maker
edge_cases.mitigation: present the accumulated artifact trail including measured drills and verified restores, state the coverage and response definitions the client can compare against, and let the decision stand without threat language or exit friction

edge_cases.description: The only realistic full recovery drill would take the client's single production server offline during trading hours
edge_cases.trigger: drill realism collides with a business that cannot pause
edge_cases.mitigation: restore into an isolated environment or outside trading hours, climb the drill ladder in stages, and record explicitly which parts of the recovery remain unrehearsed so the measured time is not overstated

workflow.action: Convert the deployment handoff into a standing response-authority envelope
workflow.description: Record the in-scope and excluded systems, the pre-authorized containment actions, the approval-required actions and the named approvers with verified after-hours contacts
workflow.artifact: signed standing authorization and response-authority document
workflow.gate: every telemetry source and every action the practice expects to take maps to a line in the envelope, and at least two approvers are reachable and verified

workflow.action: Publish the defensive boundary and the service commitment in client-facing language
workflow.description: State the prohibited actions with their refusals, the coverage window, the out-of-hours path, the response definition and target with its staffing mechanism, and the explicit exclusions
workflow.gate: the client can restate the coverage window and what happens overnight, and the response target traces to a named on-call arrangement rather than to a competitor's figure

workflow.action: Fix the status and reporting vocabulary
workflow.description: Adopt the banned-absolutes list, the evidence-bounded replacements, the ban on fear-inflated counts and the standing residual-risk sentence
workflow.artifact: claim-language standard for status, updates and reports
workflow.gate: a sample status update and report pass the absolute-claim check, carry the residual-risk sentence and state the denominator of every metric

workflow.action: Build the monitored-estate map and name the blind spots
workflow.description: Pair every asset class with a telemetry source or an accepted blind spot and set the reconciliation cadence for dead agents, unmanaged devices, stale accounts and new sites
workflow.artifact: coverage map with blind-spot list and reconciliation schedule
workflow.gate: no asset class is unaccounted for, and the first reconciliation has produced both a security finding list and a seat and site drift list

workflow.action: Tune detections for this tenant and record every suppression
workflow.description: Characterize benign-normal for this business and encode it as suppressions carrying pattern, reason, approver and expiry
workflow.gate: every active suppression has an owner and an expiry, and none covers a signal combination the declaration criteria treat as evidence of attacker access

workflow.action: Operate the triage model and measure what it costs
workflow.description: Apply the severity ordering and the fixed disposition set with written closure reasons, and capture technician minutes per tenant for the per-seat load figure
workflow.artifact: triage procedure with closure reasons and a per-tenant load measurement
workflow.gate: closures carry reasons, the out-of-hours criteria are written, and minutes per seat can be computed from the practice's own records

workflow.action: Write and rehearse the declaration criteria and the scenario runbooks
workflow.description: Define observable declaration criteria and who may declare, then write ordered first actions per realistic scenario with pre-authorized steps, evidence capture and exit criteria marked
workflow.artifact: declaration criteria and rehearsed runbook set
workflow.gate: every runbook step maps to an in-scope system and a permitted action, and each runbook has a dated tabletop walk-through

workflow.action: Establish the incident communication and escalation path
workflow.description: Name the incident lead, the client contact and their alternates, agree the out-of-band channel and update rhythm, and write the escalation triggers with routes to carrier, counsel, specialist responder and reporting channels
workflow.artifact: communication and escalation plan with verified contacts
workflow.gate: the out-of-band channel has been tested, the four-part update structure is in use, and the escalation trigger list exists with the obligation classes named as items for the client's counsel to verify

workflow.action: Assign backup verification rungs and run the first verifications
workflow.description: Give every protected data set a verification rung and cadence, verify restorability rather than job status, and review backup credential exposure and retention windows
workflow.artifact: verification schedule and dated restore-verification records
workflow.gate: each protected set has a rung and a completed dated verification, and the backup credential path and retention window are recorded

workflow.action: Run the recovery drill and publish the recoverable-set statement
workflow.description: Rehearse recovery with client participation, measure time to usable rather than time to restore, capture every failure, and write what does not come back at all
workflow.artifact: drill record with measured times, failure list and a client-facing recoverable-set statement
workflow.gate: the measured recovery times and the recoverable-set statement are in the client's hands, and every drill failure has an owner and a date

workflow.action: Run the recurring review and issue the evidence report
workflow.description: Compile coverage, hygiene, events, delivery against commitment, open risks and undone work from existing artifacts, then walk the client through the decisions
workflow.artifact: recurring evidence report and a decision list with owners
workflow.gate: every report line traces to a dated artifact, misses and undone work are included, and the review produced written decisions rather than a presentation

workflow.action: Maintain the register, map external control lists and close the renewal and growth loop
workflow.description: Keep accepted risks live and re-presented, answer questionnaires and control lists from dated evidence within the attestation boundary, and build renewal and expansion cases from observed gaps
workflow.artifact: accepted-risk register, evidence-backed control mapping and a renewal evidence pack
workflow.gate: open register entries carry decision-makers and review dates, no mapped row lacks an artifact or an honest not-in-place answer, and every expansion item cites the observation that produced it

dominance_rules.rationale: an action outside the envelope is unauthorized access regardless of how clearly it would have helped the client
dominance_rules.trigger: an incident calls for an action that is not pre-authorized or touches a system outside the envelope
dominance_rules.action: stop, reach the named approver or their alternate, record the approval, and if nobody can be reached take only the reversible in-scope actions available

dominance_rules.rule: Strictly defensive scope dominates any client demand for retaliation or third-party access
dominance_rules.rationale: offensive or unauthorized action exposes the practice and every other client it serves, and it is not the practice's to grant
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks for the attacker to be traced, accessed, or for a third party's systems to be probed
dominance_rules.action: refuse with the pre-written sentence and route to evidence preservation, law-enforcement or fraud reporting, the carrier and counsel

dominance_rules.rule: Client exposure dominates the practice's commercial interest
dominance_rules.rationale: concealment or delayed escalation converts a manageable incident into an uninsured or unreported one and destroys the relationship it was meant to protect
dominance_rules.trigger: escalating, disclosing or reporting would embarrass the practice or risk the account
dominance_rules.action: escalate and disclose on the stated trigger and rebuild the relationship afterwards with evidence

dominance_rules.rationale: an all-clear that has to be retracted costs more trust than any amount of admitted uncertainty
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks whether they are safe, clean or contained before verification is complete
dominance_rules.action: state what is known, what is not yet known, what is being done and what is needed, and defer the all-clear until it is verified

dominance_rules.rule: Reversible containment dominates irreversible remediation while the picture is incomplete
dominance_rules.rationale: a reversible action preserves both the business and the investigation, while a wipe or an overwrite forecloses both
dominance_rules.trigger: a containment choice must be made before the scope of the compromise is understood
dominance_rules.action: take the reversible option, buy time, and escalate the irreversible option to the named approver with the trade stated plainly

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence preservation dominates cleanup speed unless active harm is ongoing
dominance_rules.rationale: perishable logs and artifacts cannot be recreated, and external parties will ask what was done and on what basis
dominance_rules.trigger: a remediation step would destroy logs, rules, headers or an endpoint state
dominance_rules.action: capture the runbook's list first; if active harm makes that impossible, contain and record precisely what was lost and why

dominance_rules.rule: The stated coverage commitment dominates margin pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: silently delivering less than was promised is a misrepresentation that surfaces at the worst possible moment
dominance_rules.trigger: a tenant's measured load exceeds the labor its price funds
dominance_rules.action: tune within hygiene limits, fix or fund the underlying condition, re-scope or reprice openly, and never reduce monitored scope without a written change

dominance_rules.rule: The client's counsel, carrier and assessor dominate the practice on legal, coverage and compliance determinations
dominance_rules.rationale: these are licensed or contractual judgments the practice is neither qualified nor insured to make, and a wrong answer harms the client more than an honest gap
dominance_rules.trigger: a question arises about notification duties, policy coverage, or whether the client is compliant
dominance_rules.action: name the obligation class, state that it must be verified currently in their jurisdiction and contracts, supply the factual evidence, and route the determination to the client's own advisers

dominance_rules.rule: Calibrated evidence dominates any opportunity to sell with fear
dominance_rules.rationale: fear-based selling inside an established relationship exploits trust and destroys the client's ability to judge real risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a renewal is challenged, an expansion could be sold, or an incident makes the client receptive
dominance_rules.action: present observed evidence and residual risk in neutral language, keep offers out of live incidents, and record declines in the register without escalation

dominance_rules.rule: A documented suppression with an owner and an expiry dominates ad-hoc noise reduction
dominance_rules.rationale: an undocumented suppression is an invisible disabled detection that nobody will ever revisit
dominance_rules.trigger: a technician moves to silence a recurring alert
dominance_rules.action: record the pattern, reason, approver and expiry, and refuse the suppression outright if it would cover a declaration-criteria signal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Convert the deployment authorization into a standing response envelope with named approvers before the first alert is triaged
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-incident permission hunt, or an action taken without authority that must later be explained to the client, an insurer or a regulator

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map telemetry coverage and name the blind spots before tuning anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending weeks tuning a stream that never contained the critical source, and discovering the gap only in a post-incident timeline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every suppression with a pattern, reason, approver and expiry at the moment it is created
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invisible permanent blind spot that surfaces years later as the reason an incident was not detected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the coverage window, the response definition and the exclusions in writing before an incident tests them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a dispute in which the client believed they had bought continuous monitoring and the practice believed it had sold business-hours triage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write and rehearse the runbooks and the communication path before an incident rather than during one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: improvised communication through a compromised channel and irreversible actions taken before evidence capture

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify restorability at a stated rung before communicating any recovery expectation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: promising a recovery time that a real event proves impossible, which is the single most damaging failure in this service

anti_rework_rules.rule: Export perishable identity, mail and audit logs at declaration, before any remediation step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an investigation that can never be completed and questions from an insurer, a customer or a regulator that can never be answered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Issue the recoverable-set statement when monitoring starts and refresh it at every review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an expectation gap discovered during a loss, when the client learns for the first time that a system was never protected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the accepted-risk register current at every review with decision-makers and dates
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a post-incident argument about whether anyone ever raised the exposure, reconstructed from memory under pressure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure minutes per seat before repricing, expanding or accepting a new tenant of the same shape
anti_rework_rules.prevents: growing a structurally unprofitable account and repeating its conditions across the book

iteration_protocol.action: run the post-incident review from preserved evidence, retune detections, update the affected runbook, and record findings as owned dated items split into in-scope and new-scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: a backup verification or a recovery drill fails or takes materially longer than the last measurement
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as an incident-grade finding, repair the cause, re-test before reporting any success, and update the recoverable-set statement and the measured recovery times

iteration_protocol.trigger: reconciliation shows estate drift such as dead agents, unmanaged devices, stale accounts or an unannounced site
iteration_protocol.action: restore coverage or record an accepted blind spot, and pass the seat and site drift to the account process as a true-up input rather than absorbing it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the authorization signer, a named approver, a client incident contact or the in-scope system list changes
iteration_protocol.action: reissue the authorization envelope and re-verify the contact and out-of-band channel before the next incident relies on them

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured minutes per seat exceed the labor budget implied by the price for two consecutive periods
iteration_protocol.action: identify the underlying condition, choose openly between tuning within hygiene limits, fixing the condition, re-scoping or repricing at renewal, and never reduce monitored scope silently

iteration_protocol.trigger: a suppression reaches its expiry date or appears in an incident timeline
iteration_protocol.action: re-justify it with a named approver or remove it, and re-test the affected declaration criteria against recent data

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client's insurer questionnaire, customer security review, contract security schedule or applicable framework changes
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the mapping from current artifacts, answer unsupported rows as not in place, flag that requirements must be verified currently in the client's jurisdiction and contracts, and convert each gap into a funded offer or a register entry

iteration_protocol.trigger: a churn signal appears or the renewal window opens
iteration_protocol.action: assemble the evidence pack from the term's dated artifacts, re-present open accepted risks neutrally, state any scope or price change as a measured cost-to-serve mechanism, and prepare a clean handback if the client leaves

priority_rationale: The run-charter units come first because authorization, the defensive boundary, the coverage commitment and the claim vocabulary decide what may be done, promised and said before any alert is touched; the detection units follow because coverage must be mapped before tuning and tuning before triage, and triage load must be measured before it silently consumes the margin; the response units build on triage because declaration starts a runbook whose containment, preservation, communication and escalation steps are all bounded by the charter; the recovery units sit in parallel on the same coverage foundation because restorability must be verified and rehearsed before any recovery expectation is communicated; and the reporting and retention units come last because reviews, evidence reports, framework mappings, the accepted-risk register, renewal cases and expansion offers are all compilations of artifacts the earlier units produce, which is why a term without those artifacts arrives at renewal with nothing honest to show.
